Description: Native AWS public control sequence, SDK metadata consumers and raw wire mutations/negative transport cases; memory and retained SQLite share the same replay.

Normalization.Clock: Each source StartedAt is a manual service instant. Transport latency is removed, not retention time. All explicit request deadlines remain exact native UTC dates.
Normalization.Deadlines: FromSequence identifies the observed creation, MPU initiation, dynamic read, reduction (old-duration floor), or release instant. Days/Years use calendar AddDate. Fixed explicit dates, unchanged released floors, legal OFF presence, and missing duration after release are asserted exactly. Two-year cases cross the 2028 leap day.
Normalization.Identity: Native bucket names, version IDs and upload IDs are rebound. DeleteObjects response arrays compare unordered by key; generated marker IDs must be present.
Normalization.Checksums: Valid Content-MD5 is recomputed after resource binding; missing/invalid MD5 and SHA256 checksum headers retain native request intent. Signing payload SHA256 is not treated as an object checksum.
Normalization.Reopen: Replay-only retained boundaries precede protected metadata/deletes, active and released floors, expired metadata, null-version reads, and all pending-MPU snapshot variants.
Normalization.Projection: Request IDs, provider transport dates, latency, error prose and automatic storage checksums are not asserted. Lock field presence, HTTP statuses, service codes, error argument fields and source object bytes are asserted.

ExcludedObservations.Label: null-after-set-retention
ExcludedObservations.Reason: Isolated native post-activation result said bucket was missing Object Lock despite accepted retention, legal getter and HEAD metadata. Activation propagation is an inference, not proven. Stable first/current/later null-version retention observations 382,383,386 are replayed instead.
